page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-128GB is a Cloud Native family server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The system is configured with 16 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation model. It includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a mixed performance profile. In stress-ng single-core CPU testing, the server achieves a top-tier score of 3417.88, placing it in the top 10 percent of tested instances. However, multi-core performance in stress-ng is average at 45259.32. Geekbench testing mirrors this moderate multi-core capability, with a single-core score of 1812.0 and a multi-core score of 4526.0. Software compilation and ray tracing workloads perform in the average tier, while image processing and text processing benchmarks show weak to poor performance, scoring 2526.0 and 1132.0 respectively.

The primary architectural tradeoff of this server is its shared CPU allocation, which can introduce resource contention under sustained multi-threaded workloads, explaining the drop from top-tier single-core performance to average multi-core results. The lack of integrated local storage requires external storage provisioning. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core provides a dense memory footprint suitable for memory-intensive tasks that do not require dedicated, continuous CPU execution.

This server configuration is suited for memory-optimized workloads that can tolerate shared CPU resources, such as caching layers, in-memory databases, and moderate software compilation tasks. It is less appropriate for intensive text or image processing applications due to lower benchmark results in those specific areas.
